# Sayable

> A catalogue of domain names built only from sounds that appear in almost
> every language on earth, with availability checked against the registry.
> Names are ranked by cross-linguistic pronounceability and each carries the
> confidence level it was verified to.

If you are an AI agent, read `skill.md` first (relative to this file). It is a complete operating
guide: how to query this data, how to interpret confidence levels, and what
claims you should not make from it.

## Before you use this data

Availability has four confidence levels, and they are not interchangeable.
Only `rdap` and `registrar` mean the registry actually answered. A `dns`
result is a lead — a domain can be registered with no nameservers, and DNS
cannot see it. Never report a `dns` result as "available".

Every record carries `checked_at`. Anything older than about three weeks
should be re-verified before you rely on it.

## Data

- [/data/domains.json](data/domains.json): the full ranked snapshot. Positional
  rows; the `fields` key names the columns. Also carries the phoneme table,
  scoring constants, blocklist, and per-name meanings and alternate TLDs.
- [/data/api.json](data/api.json): machine-readable description of every
  endpoint here, including the row schema and confidence semantics.
- [/data/cmudict/index.json](data/cmudict/index.json): manifest for the
  sharded pronunciation dictionary. Shards are keyed by the first two letters
  of a word, so fetch `/data/cmudict/cl.json` for "cloud".

## Tools

- [/skill.md](skill.md): the agent skill — workflow, safety rails, and how to
  read results correctly.
- The `pdgen` CLI has a `query` subcommand that emits JSON for exactly this
  purpose: `pdgen query --available --syllables 2 --min-confidence rdap`.

## Optional

- [Source and CLI](https://github.com/KakkoiDev/sayable-domains)
